explanations.text:
import json, the pattern matcher, the shell, a lock, the clock, and two neighbours:
[the tool](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py) — the project folder, the map of a file —
and [the project hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py), which knows the word project and its map;
for a training, it also calls on [the training store](compiler/cli/human/cmd_store.py) — your login and its refusals —
and [the training hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py), which keeps one session open

FOLDER = server — the folder under human/ where a writing from the reader waits
KINDS  = the eight kinds of writing: retext, map, code, decompile, expand, create, delete, link
TRAINED = the three asks claude answers with a training: decompile, expand, create
WRITTEN = the three kinds that carry words of your own: retext, map, code
ENTRY_RE = the look of the line "entry 3: …" the map command prints, so the new number can be read back


[compile_writing](compile_writing)(root, name, kind, eid, text, words)
    root is the project folder; name is the file as the reader names it,
    like src/app.py, or the word project; kind is one of the seven the
    reader may send — every kind but link; eid is
    the entry the words replace, or the entry an ask stands on, or
    nothing; text is what you typed in the reader and sent with the
    compile button, and it may be empty on an ask; words are the words
    you highlighted in an entry for an expand.

    ●  the tool checks the ask
    │     An unknown kind stops here, and so does a link. An empty text stops the three kinds
    │     that carry your words; an ask for claude may come with no text
    │     at all. A name that is not a file of the project stops too, and
    │     so does a file under human/ — the maps take no writing. The
    │     map of the name is read ([the map of a name](map_of)) — it may
    │     not exist yet.
    │
    ●  the tool runs the same command you would have typed          ([the command run](run_cli))
    │     A rewrite of an entry runs human retext <name> <id> --verbatim:
    │     your words go in as your own, the origin is reset, and the
    │     entries that stood on the old words are marked stale. A first
    │     telling runs human map <name> --verbatim: plain words, a pin in
    │     them refused; on a file that has a map already the run stops —
    │     write on its entries instead. Code on a file with no map is
    │     written to the file as it is; on a file with a map the run stops,
    │     because the words come first there.
    │
    ●  an ask only claude can answer is queued as it stands
    │     A decompile asks for a first telling of a file: the project has
    │     no code of its own and stops, and a file that has a map stops
    │     too — expand or create on its entries. An empty file stops as
    │     well — there is no code to tell yet, so write its telling first
    │     and claude writes the code under it. A create asks for a top
    │     abstraction over an entry. An expand asks for more words under
    │     the words you highlighted, and stops when no words came with it.
    │     A create and an expand stop when the map holds no such entry.
    │     An expand sent with a text of your own runs human map <name>
    │     --verbatim first, so your words go in at once and the ask
    │     carries the new entry with it.
    │
    ●  a delete takes the entry out at once and queues nothing
    │     It stops when the map holds no such entry. Otherwise it runs
    │     human undo <name> --entry <id>: the entry leaves the map, and the
    │     run stops when another entry, or the project map, points at it
    │     through an anchor. The reader gets what the command said, joined
    │     in one line, without the line that names the written map.
    │
    ●  a refusal goes back to the reader in the command's own words
    │     The gates are the same as on the command line. Nothing is queued
    │     when a gate speaks.
    │
    ●  the tool looks for the tellings that stand on a code write        ([the pins that reach a file](pins_reaching))
    │     Every map is read for a pin that names the file. With no pin the
    │     file is saved and nothing more happens — no telling depends on
    │     it. With pins, they go into the event, so claude knows which
    │     tellings the change may have made wrong.
    │
    ●  an ask claude writes gets a training session                   ([the training of an ask](training_for))
    │     A decompile, a create, or an expand with no words of your own
    │     gets one when you are logged in: the open session of the
    │     training store, or a new one when none is open. The event
    │     carries the session number, and the output names it and says
    │     when it was opened. When the store refuses or does not answer,
    │     the event carries no session, the output says why, and the ask
    │     is queued all the same.
    │
    ●  one event joins the queue                                        ([the queue](append_event))
          The kind, the name, the absolute paths of the map and the file,
          the entry number — read from the output for a first telling —,
          the old text and the new, the pins, and what the command printed.
          An ask adds the entry it stands on as its target, an expand adds
          the highlighted words, and the output of an ask says what waits
          for claude.
          The reader gets the number of the event and the printed lines.

[cmd_watch](cmd_watch)(a)
    a is what you typed: human watch, or human watch --once.

    ●  claude arms it once per session, from the project root
    │     Every event not yet done is printed, one JSON line each, in the
    │     order it came. An event printed in an earlier session comes with
    │     replay true, so claude checks the maps before it syncs anything.
    │
    ●  the tool follows
          Every second it reads the queue again ([the events](read_events)) and prints
          what is new. The cursor's seen mark moves to the last printed
          event ([the cursor](read_cursor)). With --once it prints and stops.

[cmd_ack](cmd_ack)(a)
    a holds the number of the event claude finished: human ack 3.

    ●  the tool moves the done mark
          The number must be above the last done and not beyond the last
          event; otherwise the tool says what is done and what is last.
          Then it says how many events still wait. The reader drops the
          compiling mark of the entry when the queue tells it the event is done.

[pending](pending)(root)
    ●  the reader asks what still waits
          The done and seen marks, and one line per event above done: its
          number, kind, name, and entry. The reader polls this to mark an
          entry as compiling.

──────────────────────────────────────
the small hands

[folder](folder)(root)                        human/server/ under the root, made on first use
[events_path](events_path)(root)              the queue file, events.jsonl
[cursor_path](cursor_path)(root)              the cursor file, cursor.json
[read_events](read_events)(root)              every event of the queue, oldest first
[read_cursor](read_cursor)(root)              the done and seen marks; zero and zero when none
[write_cursor](write_cursor)(root, c)         writes the marks back
[append_event](append_event)(root, event)     numbers the event one above the last, stamps the moment, adds it
[run_cli](run_cli)(root, args, text)          runs the human command in the project folder with the text on its
                                              stdin; gives back whether it passed and what it printed
[map_of](map_of)(root, name)                  the map file of a name and its content, or nothing when there is none
[pins_reaching](pins_reaching)(root, name)    every pin of every map that names the file: the map, the entry,
                                              the words, and the block or anchor it points at
[training_for](training_for)(root, event)     ties an ask claude writes to the open training session, or opens
                                              one; says in the output which session, or why there is none
